articles.title: "I wish I had more time to give": Tom Brady's parents faced a heartbreaking reality as his first Super Bowl win changed their family life
articles.summary: Tom Brady spent years chasing the dream of becoming an NFL star. But when he finally reached the top, success brought changes that went beyond football.
articles.body: Tom Brady spent years chasing the dream of becoming an NFL star. But when he finally reached the top, success brought changes that went beyond football. His first Super Bowl victory turned him into a household name, and the attention that followed began to reshape his family life. During his New England Patriots Hall of Fame induction in June 2024, a family tribute brought back a bittersweet memory. His parents recalled how their son's growing fame changed the time they could spend together.Tom Brady's first Super Bowl win changed his family lifeBrady's rise to fame happened quickly. After joining the Patriots as a sixth-round pick in 2000, he took over as the team's starting quarterback and led them to a stunning Super Bowl victory in the 2001 season. He was no longer just the young player his family had watched grow up. He was becoming one of the biggest names in American sports.That change became clear during his first trip to the Pro Bowl after winning the championship. In a video shown during his Hall of Fame induction, Brady's parents, Tom Sr. and Galynn, looked back on the period when their son's growing profile began to affect their family routine.The report by Yahoo Sports highlighted a particularly touching detail. His parents remembered that Brady could no longer do everything with them as he once had. His sudden fame brought new demands, more people seeking his attention and less time for ordinary family moments.For parents who had supported his journey long before the trophies arrived, this was a bittersweet part of watching him succeed. His career was reaching extraordinary heights, but the simple access they once had to their son was changing.It was not a sign that Brady had forgotten his family. Rather, his growing responsibilities showed how difficult it could become to balance a demanding career with the relationships that had shaped him.Tom Brady's emotional Hall of Fame speech revealed what he missedThe family reflection also connected with Brady's own words during the June 12, 2024 ceremony. As he looked around at the people who had shared his journey, the former quarterback acknowledged that success had not always left him enough time for everyone who mattered.His voice reportedly broke as he addressed the people who had supported him throughout his two decades in New England."I wish I had more time," he said tearfully at the end of the night. "I wish I had more time to give you all."The admission gave his parents' recollection a deeper meaning. Brady had achieved almost everything an NFL player could dream of, but he recognised that time with loved ones was something no championship could replace.His story offers a reminder that sporting success can change family life in unexpected ways. For the Bradys, the first Super Bowl brought immense pride, but it also marked the beginning of a different relationship with a son whose world was growing far beyond home.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New Daniel Jones Rumors Uncover Buzz Surrounding QB's Surprising Colts Release During NFL Season
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday, but some people within the organization reportedly believed the signal-caller would have requested his release soon enough, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on the latest edition of SportsCenter.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday, but some people within the organization reportedly believed the signal-caller would have requested his release soon enough, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on the latest edition of SportsCenter .

"It's a combination of poor play, the money he's due (around $10 million in a 2027 injury guarantee), so they get him off the books, they don't have to worry about that," Fowler said.

"They take all the guesswork out. And then also there's a feeling in that building from some that Daniel Jones did want out. Shane Steichen today said that Jones never requested to be released, but talking to people there in Indianapolis, they believed that he was at least thinking about it or wanted to be out or was maybe going to request that early next week.

"So the Colts get ahead of all that, and they turn to Anthony Richardson, who is 8-7 as a starter, but what complicates it is talking to people there, I never got the sense that the Colts were planning to go to Richardson. This is sort of a sudden move with some other implications. Now they need to work with him, somebody who's very talented, but needs a resurgence after a couple down years of getting benched back in 2024."

This has been a difficult season for Jones and the 3-8 Colts. In 11 starts, Jones has thrown nearly twice as many interceptions (13) as touchdowns (seven).

The interception number leads the NFL. Jones' 58.4 percent completion rate, 5.6 yards per attempt and 65.4 quarterback rating are all career-low marks for the eight-year veteran.

Indianapolis has also lost six of its last seven games, with the lone exception being a 24-22 home win over the 1-8 Miami Dolphins. The Colts previously parted ways with general manager Chris Ballard. and conducted a midseason fire sale as well.

The Colts reportedly received trade interest in Jones, per ESPN's Adam Schefter, but turned it down.

Jones arrived in Indianapolis in 2025 on a one-year, $14 million contract . He was sensational over the first eight games of the season, completing 71.2 percent of his passes for 13 touchdowns (three interceptions) and 2,062 yards while guiding Indianapolis to a 7-1 record.

Jones encountered more struggles in his final five games of the season, and unfortunately, his 2025 campaign ended after he suffered a torn Achilles against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 14.

Jones returned to Indianapolis on a two-year, $88 million contract, and his rehab progressed well enough for him to return for Week 1. However, Jones took a step back in 2026. The Colts will also take a big dead cap hit.

Indianapolis is undergoing a significant rebuild at this juncture. It's unclear, at this point, who the general manager, head coach and QB1 of this team will be in 2027.

It was likely safe to assume that Jones would not be the team's starting quarterback next year. However, the process has accelerated, and now the Colts turn to Richardson in the meantime. Meanwhile, Jones is free to join another team in free agency assuming he clears waivers on Monday.

articles.title: Myles Garrett carries his late friend's memory into every game as emotional 'Live Like Luke' tribute honours the college teammate he lost to cancer
articles.summary: For Myles Garrett, one of the most meaningful things he carries onto a football field is not a helmet, a trophy or a piece of protective equipment.
articles.body: For Myles Garrett, one of the most meaningful things he carries onto a football field is not a helmet, a trophy or a piece of protective equipment. It is a small blue wristband bearing the words “Live Like Luke.” The Cleveland Browns star wears it every day to remember Luke Laufenberg, his former Texas A&M teammate who died at 21 after battling an aggressive form of cancer. Their time together ended far too soon, but Garrett has never allowed that friendship to become just a memory. Through personal tributes and charitable support, he continues to share the story of a young man whose outlook on life left a lasting mark on him.Myles Garrett's wristband keeps his late friend close every daySome friendships leave a mark that time cannot erase. For Garrett, Luke's place in his life is reflected in a simple ritual that has stayed with him long after their college days ended.“This wristband is on 24/7,” Garrett said, describing the blue band that carries Luke's name and message. It is not something he wears only during games or special occasions. The wristband remains a constant reminder of the person behind it.The two met at Texas A&M, where Garrett was already making a name for himself as a powerful defensive player. Luke, meanwhile, joined the football programme as a walk-on tight end. His role often put him on the opposite side of Garrett during practice, where he had to block the future NFL star on the scout team.Their positions may have been different, but football gave them a chance to build a friendship. Garrett remembers more than the time they spent on the field. He remembers Luke's willingness to help people and his habit of putting others first.“He was always asking me, ‘What do you need? I’ll do that, I’ll be that,’” Garrett recalled.That question offers a glimpse into the kind of person Luke was. He did not need a big platform to make a difference. He simply looked for ways to support the people around him. Garrett has carried that lesson with him, turning a personal reminder into a way to encourage others to live with the same generosity.Luke Laufenberg's cancer battle left a lasting impact on Myles GarrettLuke's life changed in 2017, when he was diagnosed with Burkitt lymphoma, a rare and aggressive form of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. He was only 19. The diagnosis came just months after he had celebrated Garrett's selection by the Cleveland Browns as the first overall pick in the 2017 NFL Draft.The illness brought a difficult fight, but Luke continued to show the spirit that had drawn people towards him. His battle lasted less than two years. He died in 2019, aged 21, leaving his family, teammates and friends to deal with a loss that came far too early.For Garrett, remembering Luke means looking beyond the illness and the painful circumstances of his death. He wants people to know the person who lived with courage, optimism and a desire to make others better.That is why the words “Live Like Luke” carry so much meaning. They are not simply a slogan printed on a wristband. They reflect the qualities Garrett saw in his friend and wants others to carry into their own lives.“Optimistic, resilient, just always wanted to be the one percent better, make people around him a little bit better just for knowing him and that wasn't his goal or mission but just the kind of person he was. I think we all could live like that,” Garrett said.Luke's approach to life also gives Garrett a different way to measure success. Football offers records, awards and public recognition. But the influence one person has on others can last much longer than a season. Luke's example continues to shape how Garrett thinks about friendship, kindness and responsibility.Myles Garrett honours Luke Laufenberg with emotional cleats tributeGarrett found another way to make Luke's story visible during the NFL's My Cause My Cleats campaign in November 2025. The initiative gives players an opportunity to use custom footwear to highlight causes that matter to them.Garrett chose the Luke Laufenberg Fight Fund. His cleats featured Luke's portrait against a blue, sky-inspired background, along with the hashtag #LiveLikeLuke. The design brought a deeply personal story onto a national football stage.The tribute also gave Garrett a chance to reconnect with memories from college. He had met Jason Garrett and shared a photograph with him, which brought back emotions from the time he spent with Luke. The moment helped inspire his decision to make the tribute more visible.“Well, I got the chance to meet with Jason Garrett, and we took a picture and sent it to Babe, and kind of brought back that emotion back of that time when we were in college and we were spending time on the field, time after school and after practice together, just bringing back those memories. I always wear his wristband, reminding me of and the kind of person that he is.”Garrett also explained why he wanted to bring Luke's story to a wider audience.“I just wanted to bring it full circle and show how much he left an impression on all of us, including myself and he's a hell of a person and I'm better because I knew him,” Garrett said.The cleats meant more than a visual tribute. They gave fans a chance to learn about a young athlete whose life had touched one of the NFL's biggest defensive stars. They also helped direct attention towards a cause that carries Luke's name.Luke Laufenberg Fight Fund turns his memory into support for othersThe most meaningful part of Garrett's tribute may be the work that continues beyond the football field. The Luke Laufenberg Fight Fund was established in Luke's honour at the University of Texas at El Paso. It supports student-athletes who share the qualities that defined him, including determination, generosity and a willingness to help others.The fund gives Garrett a way to turn remembrance into practical support. Instead of allowing Luke's story to remain limited to old photographs and memories, the initiative helps provide resources for young athletes who are building their own futures.Garrett has also spoken about how Luke's habit of looking out for others could inspire a wider change in everyday life.“Luke was always reaching out and seeing what another person needed,” Garrett said. “If everyone did that, the world would be a much better place.”That message is at the heart of the #LiveLikeLuke tribute. It asks people to notice those around them, offer help when they can and make an effort to leave others better than they found them.For Garrett, the wristband remains the most personal part of the tribute. The custom cleats brought Luke's face before a much larger audience, while the fund helps keep his values active in the lives of young athletes.A football career is often measured by what a player achieves on the field. Garrett's tribute tells another story. It shows how a friendship can continue to influence someone long after a final practice or game. Luke Laufenberg did not get the chance to see where life would take his college teammate, but his spirit remains part of Garrett's journey.Every time Garrett looks at that blue wristband, he has a reminder of what truly matters. And every time he shares Luke's story, he gives others a reason to remember him, too.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

Jim Nantz Says CBS Was Right To Lock In J.J. Watt

In an interview with Front Office Sports, Michael McCarthy asked Nantz whether CBS executive David Berson's quick move to name Watt as Tony Romo's permanent replacement helped the network avoid the drama now engulfing ESPN.

"I'm happy that they made that call as a permanent call. I think the viewing audience sees J.J. as someone who has a lot of talent. And a lot of passion," Nantz said .

"Power and passion together are a pretty powerful punch—speaking of punches. Just a great team guy. So I'm thrilled that David put that to rest when he did. I mean, why play this out?" he asked.

CBS announced Watt's multiyear agreement Oct. 22. He will keep calling the network's top NFL games with Nantz and sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson, and the deal includes Super Bowl LXII in Atlanta in 2028.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker III's second straight absence raises questions about Chiefs' backfield plans ahead of crucial Bills showdown
articles.summary: Kenneth Walker III will miss Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
articles.body: Kenneth Walker III will miss Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals. The Chiefs ruled out their lead running back Friday because of a groin injury, and it is his second straight absence. Walker did not practice all week. He was leading the AFC in rushing when he got hurt against the Jets on Nov. 8. Rookie Emmett Johnson will start again. The bigger picture is the calendar. Kansas City plays Buffalo on Thanksgiving night, just four days after Arizona, and the Chiefs look willing to give up a soft Sunday to get Walker right for that one.Kenneth Walker misses a second game with a groin injuryThe Chiefs have been careful with this injury from the start. Kenneth Walker sat out last week's 35-13 win at Atlanta, and on Wednesday Andy Reid said the team would not make any declarations about his status for Sunday. The coach sounded more worried about a setback than a timeline. “You don’t want to do something stupid,” Reid said. “He’s feeling a lot better than he was.”Friday brought the official word, reported by Adam Schefter. Walker is 26 and leads the Chiefs with 11 total touchdowns. He has five 100-yard games and 872 rushing yards. That is a lot of production to set aside, which makes the patience stand out. The offense still scored 35 without him last week, which is part of why this looks like caution, not alarm.Arizona makes that patience easy. The Cardinals are banged up at receiver and quarterback, and rookie Carson Beck got hurt Friday too. A division rival would probably have drawn a questionable tag for Walker. Against this opponent, the Chiefs can sit him without much worry.There is a cost to this plan. Johnson is still a rookie, and Atlanta gave defenses real film on him. Arizona will see it, and so will Buffalo. The Chiefs are betting that a fifth-round pick can keep producing once opponents know what he does well.Johnson gives Kansas City room to waitThe rookie has earned that room. articles.title: Daniel Jones' nearly $167 million NFL fortune reveals how much he has earned despite uncertainty surrounding his career
articles.summary: Daniel Jones has been waived by the Indianapolis Colts, but his bank account is in good shape.
articles.body: Daniel Jones has been waived by the Indianapolis Colts, but his bank account is in good shape. Over The Cap lists his career NFL earnings at $166.9 million across stints with the Giants, Vikings and Colts. The Colts released him on Friday, one day after a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans. Jones completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards and an interception before Anthony Richardson took over. Richardson will start against the New York Giants on Nov. 29. At 29, Jones now faces an open question about where he plays next.Daniel Jones' nearly $167 million NFL fortune and what it says about his careerJones was the sixth overall pick in the 2019 draft, and the Giants gave him a four-year rookie deal worth $25.66 million. After the 2022 season, New York raised the stakes with a four-year, $160 million extension.Headlines said $160 million. The cash said otherwise. The Giants moved on after two seasons, and Over The Cap puts his earnings under that extension at about $46 million. Then came the part many fans forget. Spotrac says New York paid him another $36 million in 2024 after waiving him that November.Minnesota was a short stop. Indianapolis was the reset. Jones signed a one-year, $14 million deal for 2025 and threw for 3,101 yards, 19 touchdowns and eight interceptions in 13 games. It was one of the most productive years of his career, and the Colts paid for it with a two-year, $88 million contract. Nearly $50 million was fully guaranteed, and incentives could lift the value to $100 million.Add the $160 million and the $88 million and you get $248 million. That is not what Jones earned. His career has had more swings than most, and two teams have now cut him. Each exit still came with real money.Jones' Colts contract left a $49.8 million bill for a 3-8 seasonThis season went the other way. Jones went 3-8 as the starter, with 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns and 13 interceptions. Spotrac says the Colts will have paid about $49.8 million for his work in 2026. That is a steep bill for a quarterback who lost his job during a losing year.The guarantees explain why. With nearly $50 million fully guaranteed, benching or cutting him did not erase what the Colts owed.Dead cap is where it lingers. Indianapolis is projected to carry $14.89 million for Jones in 2026 and $35.2 million in 2027. Those are cap accounting figures, not new payments to him.Football is only part of the picture. Forbes lists Nike, FedEx, Amazon Data Centers, Fanatics, Hugo Boss, Panini, Raising Cane's, United Airlines and Verizon among his sponsors. The value of those deals is not public, so the NFL total should not be treated as his net worth.Jones is 29, and another contract is possible. Teams will weigh his 2025 numbers against this year's. Whether anyone wants him as a starter is the unanswered part. The money, at least, is settled.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sam Hartman plans to study The Bachelor like NFL game film after admitting he has never watched an episode
articles.summary: Sam Hartman has spent years preparing for football games by studying film, but his next assignment calls for different homework.
articles.body: Sam Hartman has spent years preparing for football games by studying film, but his next assignment calls for different homework. The Washington Commanders quarterback, set to lead the next season of ABC’s The Bachelor, admitted he has never watched an episode of the long-running dating show. Hartman told reporters on Thursday, Nov. 19, that he plans to catch up after the NFL regular season, using the same detailed approach he brings to the field. Until then, he says, football remains his priority.Sam Hartman plans to study The Bachelor like game film“I haven’t seen an episode,” Hartman said after the Commanders’ Thursday practice, referring to all 29 seasons of The Bachelor. That leaves the 27-year-old with plenty of viewing to do before filming begins after the NFL regular season.He plans to use the tools he knows best. “I’m going to probably do some tape-watching after the season is over and study up,” Hartman said. He described the plan in football terms: “get the DVSport clicker going, you know, kind of break down first down, second down, third down and finally end at the fantasy suite.”Hartman sees the programme as more than a TV detour. He called it “an exciting opp to showcase who I am on TV” and said he hopes to find “my future teammate for life.”Asked whether love can come from a reality show, Hartman said yes. He turned the question back on the reporter before making his point: “no matter how you meet somebody,” what matters is whether you want to be with that person.The Commanders quarterback says he wants to be himselfHartman has been open about the nerves that come with the assignment. His casting was announced during a live appearance on Good Morning America on Nov. 13. Asked how he felt, he replied: “[I’m] very nervous,” before adding, “I have a tough time holding a conversation with one girl; 30 is gonna be pretty tough.”He told reporters that he had informed his Commanders teammates about the show around two weeks before the announcement. “Respect to my teammates for keeping it on the down low,” he said. Their reactions have included “a lot of really, really bad advice and some good advice.”Hartman did not identify the bad suggestions. The useful guidance was to enjoy the experience and remain authentic. He said putting on a front would be the worst approach, particularly with so many people watching.His idea of a suitable partner comes back to values. Hartman said his mother is a nurse and that he hopes to meet someone who “has a lot of compassion and shares that kind of love for giving back to people, and ultimately giving back to each other.”He has said he is “super-focused on football” until the season ends. Former NFL players Rob Gronkowski and Julian Edelman have questioned the timing of his Bachelor promotion during the season, but Hartman says football comes first. He wants to finish the season before turning to the cameras.Hartman knows the show will bring scrutiny, much as his career has brought praise and criticism. His aim is to find a lasting relationship rather than simply make television. He joked that he hopes to find a second love while continuing to show that person his first love: football.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith Is That Good, So Which NFL Teams Could Consider Trading Up for Star WR in 2027 Draft
articles.summary: Calvin Johnson, AJ Green, Julio Jones and Ja'Marr Chase are the best wide receiver prospects over the last 25 years. None of them were the No. 1 overall pick in their respective draft classes. Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith is on par with all four as a prospect and possibly even better. NFL teams should be falling over themselves to try to acquire his services.
articles.body:
Calvin Johnson, AJ Green, Julio Jones and Ja'Marr Chase are the best wide receiver prospects over the last 25 years. None of them were the No. 1 overall pick in their respective draft classes. Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith is on par with all four as a prospect and possibly even better. NFL teams should be falling over themselves to try to acquire his services.

Currently, Smith holds the highest grade the Bleacher Report Scouting Report has ever assigned in its seven cycles of evaluating collegiate talent. At 9.9 (out of 10), the wide receiver is considered a near-perfect prospect.

Take a quick look at Smith's scouting report , courtesy of B/R's Dame Parson , and realize he's the ideal NFL receiver. Here are the highlights:

NFL body, frame and sturdy build to create advantageous physical matchups. - Intentional route-runner with violent steps and snappiness out of his breaks. - Powerful strider with top-end speed to attack and exploit the vertical plane. - Incredible strength and reliable hands; rarely drops passes. - Outstanding ball-tracking down the field, shows late hands and reaches another level of aggressiveness once the ball is in the air.

Smith already broke the Big Ten Conference's all-time receiving yardage and touchdown records before his true junior season had even come to a close.

With a quarterback almost certainly going No. 1 overall due to demand at the position, Smith's skill set should be up for sale, with numerous organizations jockeying to trade up for a pass-catcher. The Los Angeles Chargers, who currently own next year's second overall pick, could easily select Smith and happily move on without thinking twice. Or, the organization can get a windfall of draft picks to address multiple roster issues and kickstart the team's rebuild. Five specific franchises are within striking distance based on the current draft order that should be desperate to trade up for Smith.

Current Draft Slot : Third overall The Miami Dolphins could find themselves in a difficult position based on how the draft order currently sits. Everything will depend on how the organization wants to move forward at quarterback. Malik Willis was placed in a near-impossible position this season due to the lack of talent around the quarterback position. Injuries have only made the situation worse. Willis now finds himself on injured reserve. The Dolphins have two pathways to pursue this offseason. Either the front office builds around Willis, or the team chooses to go all-in on another quarterback. Miami could easily be the franchise trying to move up for the No. 1 overall pick to draft Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker. If that doesn't happen, the Dolphins' decision-makers should do everything in their power to obtain Smith, even if that means swapping picks to move up one spot. Miami drafted three wide receivers in this year's class, but the team can't stop there since none of them should be considered legitimate No. 1 targets. Whatever the Dolphins eventually do at quarterback, a weapon of Smith's caliber will greatly help whoever is behind center. Furthermore, Miami's lineup simply needs a playmaker and an infusion of talent. Thus, drafting arguably the best wide receiver prospect of all time should be a priority.

Current Draft Slot : Fifth overall Should Philadelphia Eagles general manager Howie Roseman trade up to draft a wide receiver for a third time? Yes. That idea isn't an indictment of DeVonta Smith or rookie Makai Lemon. Instead, the approach is all about taking advantage of a significant opportunity if it's presented. Due to this season going off the rails, the Eagles currently own a top-five draft pick. Philadelphia hasn't selected that high since trading up for Carson Wentz in the 2016 class. In fact, Roseman isn't shy about making a move, even if it's a minimal trade-up, to ensure the team lands a specific talent. See: Carter, Jalen. Much like Carter, Jeremiah Smith can completely change the complexion of the Eagles' roster, especially on offense. What the team lost when it traded AJ Brown can be reinserted with a younger, more explosive version. Thus, a trio of Jeremiah Smith, DeVonta Smith and Lemon will be extremely difficult to defend, with each placed in specific roles to maximize their skill sets. Furthermore, the Eagles still don't know exactly how they'll progress at quarterback beyond this position. If Jalen Hurts is medically cleared and ready to return, more weapons in the passing game will help prevent the intermittent offensive stagnation that has plagued the Eagles during the last two seasons. Even without Hurts, a wide receiver corps consisting of those three targets will make anyone better.

The Washington Commanders' offseason plan should be relatively simple: Do whatever is necessary to improve Jayden Daniels' surrounding cast. A legitimate No. 1 target can only help the young quarterback's development.

Stefon Diggs currently leads the Commanders with 36 receptions for 386 yards. Those numbers rank 43rd and 50th overall, respectively. Washington's top wide receiver, Terry McLaurin, is already out for the season with a torn patellar tendon, a difficult injury from which to bounce back, particularly for a 31-year-old wide receiver. Furthermore, four of the team's wide receivers—Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown, Van Jefferson and Diggs, who turns 33 next weekend—are free agents after this season.

Washington requires a reset among its skill positions. Jeremiah Smith is the perfect piece to serve as the starting point.

However, the Commanders' front office may have agreed upon a significant deal to target the class's WR1 since Washington currently sits just outside the 2027 draft's Top 10. Deals of this nature have happened before. A handful of teams may consider a talent of Smith's caliber. However, a pair of first-round picks will likely be the starting point for any conversation. He's worth it, though.

Current Draft Slot : 14th overall The Baltimore Ravens are losing ground in the AFC North and the conference itself. At the same time, a down season should serve as a chance for self-reflection. An injury to quarterback Lamar Jackson certainly hasn't helped matters. Even so, the Ravens must consider a change in their approach. Running back Derrick Henry turns 33 in January. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley, who also turns 33 next year, is no longer playing at a Pro Bowl-caliber level. Tight end Mark Andrews will turn 32 during the 2027 season. A handful of other aging veterans are pending free agents as well. Next offseason will be the ideal time for the organization to reassess its setup and head in a different direction. To do so, the team must add legitimate talent. Zay Flowers is an excellent wide receiver. He currently ranks 12th overall with 688 receiving yards despite the Ravens' starting four different quarterbacks. However, Flowers has some limitations due to his size and build. A strong move to trade up for Jeremiah Smith will finally give Jackson two big-time options in the passing game. Jackson's mobility will always be a part of his game. However, the team's continued run-first mentality hasn't allowed it to achieve anything of significance.

Instead, the Ravens could finally open up their offense to a greater degree. A trade-up for Smith will certainly make a statement. That version of the Ravens won't be the same ol' Ravens. The franchise will finally be going in a new direction and placing more emphasis on Jackson.

A strong start to the season has placed the Las Vegas Raiders further down the draft order than what's usually seen. However, the team lost six of its last seven games and moved on from veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins in favor of this year's No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza.

The latter point is important because the rookie will face multiple top defenses during Las Vegas' next seven games—which means a turnaround could be difficult. Mendoza's maturation is also crucial to the Raiders' long-term organizational health. The Raiders' current wide receiver options are underwhelming at best. Tight end Brock Bowers is the team's No. 1 receiving threat, of course. The thought of Bowers playing alongside Jeremiah Smith would be straight nightmare fuel for opposing defensive coordinators. Thus, general manager John Spytek should be ultra-aggressive and go all in to help the reigning Heisman Trophy winner and his team reach its full potential. A possible trade-up may not be quite as expensive depending on how the rest of the Raiders' season goes. Their draft slotting could easily end up around the 10th overall pick. Even so, some type of move will be necessary for Smith. The Raiders may be missing pieces at other positions, but a set of triplets featuring Mendoza, Bowers and Smith could be absolutely dynamic.

articles.title: Week 11 Waiver Wire Targets to Replace Fantasy Players on Injury List
articles.summary: Week 11 began with a blowout Houston Texans win over the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night. Many fantasy football managers could be facing an outcome similar to Indianapolis' without finding some help on the waiver wire.
articles.body:
Week 11 began with a blowout Houston Texans win over the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night. Many fantasy football managers could be facing an outcome similar to Indianapolis' without finding some help on the waiver wire.

The Colts' roster took a massive hit when the team decided to trade away Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Josh Downs, and Keenan Allen. A lot of fantasy rosters have been depleted by injuries and a massive six-team bye week.

The Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams, New England Patriots, and Seattle Seahawks have Week 11 off.

Here, we'll dive into the Week 11 injury report , provide rankings for the top remaining point-per-reception (PPR) plays, and highlight sleepers who may still be available on the waiver wire ahead of the remaining schedule.

On the injury front, Baker Mayfield is the big question mark at quarterback. He's dealing with a foot injury but practiced on Friday and appears more likely than not to start on Sunday.

The Patriots are off this week, and the Colts have already played. However, both teams have quarterback situations that should interest managers looking ahead.

Indianapolis has released Daniel Jones and will turn to backup Anthony Richardson. Drake Maye is expected to miss the rest of the season with a fractured fibula, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter , meaning New England will rely on Tommy DeVito for the foreseeable future.

Richardson and DeVito are each rostered in roughly one percent of fantasy leagues.

Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms, which means the Arizona Cardinals may turn to recently-added journeyman Josh Johnson.

Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward is rostered in only 38 percent of fantasy leagues and remains the top QB to target on the wire. The Titans haven't been good this season, but Ward has started to shine.

The second-year quarterback has been given more control of the offense and more responsibility in recent weeks. He has also used his legs more, and as a result, he has topped 20 fantasy points in his last two games.

This week, Ward will face a Dallas Cowboys team that is searching for answers defensively. Dallas' defense could be better after handing play-calling duties to Mike Pettine, but the change may not be significant.

To this point, the Cowboys have surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks. Aaron Rodgers, Jacoby Brissett, and J.J. McCarthy are second-tier targets who should be available.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

The Kansas City Chiefs have ruled out Kenneth Walker III, meaning Emmett Johnson will start for the second straight week. Jonathon Brooks, Tyjae Spears, and Will Shipley are among those listed as questionable.

San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black does not have an ideal matchup this week. San Francisco will face the Minnesota Vikings, who have surrendered the sixth-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs in 2026.

However, Black should see a significant role, even as a change-of-pace behind starter Christian McCaffrey. The rookie has logged at least 11 carries in three straight games, and he's topped 10 fantasy points in two of the three. His ceiling may be limited against Minnesota, but managers will struggle to find a higher floor on the wire.

Black is rostered in 43 percent of fantasy leagues. Samaje Perine, Kenny Gainwell, and Justice Hill are other backup RBs to consider.

The Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys have ruled out receivers Dontayvion Wicks and Jonathan Mingo, respectively. The New York Jets have ruled out Omar Cooper Jr., while the Minnesota Vikings have ruled out Jordan Addison.

Mike Evans, Ladd McConkey, Carnell Tate, Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson, and Zavion Thomas are among those listed as questionable.

While Jaylen Waddle (concussion) appears set to return for the Denver Broncos, Pat Bryant still figures to play a large role in the offense. He returned from his own injury in Week 9 and finished with 15.6 fantasy points.

This week, Bryant will face a Las Vegas Raiders defense that has surrendered the seventh-most fantasy points to opposing receivers. He's still only rostered in 21 percent of fantasy leagues.

Washington Commanders rookie receiver Antonio Williams doesn't have as favorable of a matchup. However, he should see a lot of work against a Cincinnati Bengals team that can run up the score.

Williams has reached double-digit fantasy points in two of his last three games and is only rostered in 29 percent of fantasy leagues. Makai Lemon, Ryan Flournoy, Caleb Douglas, Elic Ayomanor, Tre' Harris, and Adonai Mitchell are other receivers to consider this week.

Chigoziem Okonkwo, Washington Commanders

The Cowboys have ruled out tight end Jake Fersuon and have listed Luke Schoonmaker as questionable. Brock Bowers, Charlie Kolar, Tommy Tremble, and Darren Waller are also questionable.

The big news at tight end, though, is that Buffalo Bills standout Dalton Kincaid is now doubtful with thumb and ankle injuries. That could make Dawson Knox, who is rostered in one percent of leagues, a viable sleeper.

As previously mentioned, the Commanders will probably need to chase points against Cincinnati on Monday night. That should lead to a lot of passing by Jayden Daniels and a high-volume role for tight end Chigoziem Okonkwo.

Okonkwo finished with only four catches and 6.4 fantasy points last week. However, he was targeted eight times. He should have a better outing against a Bengals defense that has surrendered the ninth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends this season.

The 27-year-old is rostered in 46 percent of fantasy leagues. Mike Gesicki, Darren Waller, and Michael Mayer are other TEs to consider this week.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Patriots WR AJ Brown to miss multiple weeks with hamstring injury
articles.summary: New England Patriots wide receiver AJ Brown is expected to miss multiple weeks with a hamstring injury. This is his third injury of the season.
articles.body:
The injury news is getting worse for the New England Patriots . Quarterback Drake Maye is already in danger of missing most, if not all, of the regular season with a fractured fibula. Now, the Patriots will be without their top receiver, AJ Brown, for multiple weeks with a hamstring injury.

This is Brown's third injury this season, after he suffered a high ankle sprain in the season opener that landed him on injured reserve. After that, he had a knee injury that cost him another two weeks. It is unclear exactly how long Brown will be out with this injury.

At a minimum, he will miss their Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Chargers and Week 13 game versus the Buffalo Bills, since New England is on bye in Week 11. Los Angeles finally won a game and may be getting back on track, while the Bills are one of the hottest teams in the NFL right now.

Losing Maye and Brown severely hurts the Patriots' playoff chances. They are currently the No. 8 seed in the AFC, one game behind the 6-4 Cleveland Browns . The Houston Texans are also close behind New England at 4-6 and have one of the easiest remaining schedules in the NFL.

articles.title: Cowboys legend Tony Dorsett opens new exhibit at Football Hall of Fame
articles.summary: The area around Pittsburgh has produced so many who changed the game, including 23 Hall of Famers. Tony Dorsett represented them on Friday.
articles.body:
A new exhibit at the Pro Football Hall of Fame is recognizing one small pocket of the country that has churned out a staggering number of the sport's all-time greats, and they hand-picked one of the Cowboys ' biggest legends to do the honors of opening it to the public.

Tony Dorsett, the four-time Pro Bowler who spent 11 spectacular seasons in the Cowboys backfield, was in Canton on Friday for the official ribbon-cutting ceremony to open "Western PA Proud!" The special exhibit, expected to remain at the Hall until spring, celebrates the individuals, teams, and communities from the Pittsburgh area who have impacted the game in immeasurable ways over the years.

Dorsett hails from Hopewell Township, northwest of Pittsburgh, and became a Heisman Trophy winner, a national champion, and a four-time All-American for the hometown Pitt Panthers. Dorsett was then selected second overall by the Cowboys in 1977's draft and went on to help guide the team to two Super Bowl appearances and one Lombardi Trophy, leaving in 1988 as- at the time- the franchise's rushing leader, with just over 12,000 yards.

Among Dorsett's many accolades is one notable record that can never be broken. He was the first player in the NFL to record a 99-yard touchdown run, during a 1983 game (and despite the Cowboys having just 10 men on the field). It remains the longest run from scrimmage in league history and stood alone in that spotlight until Derrick Henry tied the feat with a 99-yarder of his own in 2018.

Dorsett was enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame as part of the Class of 1994. He went into the Cowboys Ring of Honor the same year. Thirty-plus years later, Dorsett, now 72, is still 11th on the NFL's all-time rushing leaderboard.

But Dorsett is far from the only Western Pennsylvania product to put his immortal stamp on the NFL. The new exhibit also recognizes George Blanda, Jim Kelly, Dan Marino, Joe Montana, Joe Namath, and Johnny Unitas- six of the greatest quarterbacks to ever play the game- all of whom, incredibly, grew up in the same geographical area. The Rooney family, who founded the Pittsburgh Steelers in 1933, as well as former NFLers Ty Law, Darrelle Revis, and onetime Cowboys player and assistant coach Mike Ditka are also prominently featured among the region's legendary figures.

In all, an astonishing 23 individuals from Western Pennsylvania are enshrined in the Hall of Fame.

Dorsett's Heisman Trophy as well as his Panthers national championship ring will be among the items displayed at the exhibit. "Western PA Proud!" will run at the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton until April 5.
